display_name: Jai Singh I & Shivaji at Purandar, 1665
one_line: Mirza Raja Jai Singh I, a Rajput Mughal general, and Shivaji, the Maratha leader, facing each other during the siege of Purandar in 1665.

appearance.age_look: Jai Singh appears in his late 50s with a solid, dignified build; Shivaji appears in his mid-30s, lean and athletic.
appearance.face: Jai Singh has a broad oval face with a medium wheat complexion, thick arched brows, a neatly trimmed full moustache and short beard along the jaw, deep-set calm eyes, and a composed, strategic default expression; Shivaji has a sharp oval face with a warm brown complexion, straight defined brows, expressive narrow eyes, a thin sharp moustache with a small pointed beard, and a focused yet restrained default expression that mixes resolve with caution.
appearance.hair: Jai Singh’s hair is black with a few silver strands, tied in a topknot hidden under a tall orange Rajput-style turban with a pleated front, a white cloth band, and a single small white egret plume on the left; Shivaji’s black hair is pulled back under a white Maratha-style pagdi (turban) with faint gold edging and a neatly wrapped tail at the back, with short sideburns visible before the ears.
appearance.costume: Jai Singh wears a long, knee-length Mughal-Rajput angarkha of finely woven off-white cotton with a subtle vertical stripe weave, crossing left over right and tied with inner cords, over a deep maroon sleeveless quilted chihnchah-style coat with small diamond stitching and a slightly flared skirt, paired with slim mustard-yellow churidar trousers gathered at the ankles and soft brown leather mojari shoes; over his shoulders is a light saffron shawl with thin red borders draped from left shoulder across the torso; around his waist is a broad dark red cloth kamarband with a hint of gold thread, and he wears a simple steel armlet on his right arm and a modest string of dark prayer beads around his neck; Shivaji wears a knee-length white cotton jama/angarkha in Deccan style with overlapping front panels, tied at the right side, decorated with a narrow golden-yellow border along the edges and cuffs, over a fitted sleeveless off-white quilted cotton vest hinted beneath the jama opening, paired with tight rust-orange churidar trousers and dark brown leather sandals; a saffron patka (waist sash) with thin green stripes is wrapped snugly around his waist with one end hanging down the left hip, and he wears a long, simple rudraksha-style bead necklace, small gold stud earrings, and plain iron armlets on both arms.
appearance.signature: Jai Singh carries at his left side a sheathed, gently curving talwar with a steel hilt and disc pommel tucked into his dark red cloth kamarband, while Shivaji carries at his left side a sheathed straight-edged Maratha sword with a simple steel hilt tucked into his saffron patka, and in his right hand he holds a rolled parchment map or farman as a symbol of the treaty negotiations.

ref_desc: Jai Singh I is an older broad-built Rajput in an off-white angarkha, maroon quilted coat, mustard churidar, saffron shawl, orange turban and talwar, facing a lean mid-30s Shivaji in a white gold-edged jama, rust-orange churidar, saffron patka, white turban, Maratha sword and rolled parchment, all in warm saffron, maroon and off-white tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of two fixed characters standing together at Purandar: on the left Mirza Raja Jai Singh I, an older broad-built Rajput general with a wheat complexion, deep-set calm eyes, thick brows, and a neat moustache with short beard, wearing a finely woven off-white knee-length angarkha crossing left over right, over a deep maroon sleeveless quilted coat with diamond stitching and slightly flared skirt, mustard-yellow churidar trousers gathered at the ankles, soft brown leather mojari shoes, a light saffron shawl draped from his left shoulder across his torso, a broad dark red cloth kamarband at his waist, a simple steel armlet and dark prayer beads, and a tall orange Rajput turban with a pleated front, white band and a single white egret plume, with a sheathed gently curving talwar with steel hilt and disc pommel tucked into his kamarband; on the right Shivaji, a lean mid-30s Maratha leader with a warm brown complexion, sharp oval face, narrow intense eyes, straight brows, thin sharp moustache and small pointed beard, wearing a knee-length white cotton Deccan jama with overlapping front panels tied on the right and edged with narrow golden-yellow borders, a hint of an off-white quilted vest visible beneath, tight rust-orange churidar trousers, dark brown leather sandals, a saffron patka with thin green stripes wrapped at the waist with one end hanging at the left hip, a long rudraksha-style bead necklace, small gold stud earrings, plain iron armlets, and a white Maratha turban with faint gold edging and a wrapped tail, carrying a sheathed straight-edged Maratha sword in his patka and holding a rolled parchment map or farman in his right hand; show them front-facing with clear views of face, hair, turbans, garments, sashes, jewellery, swords and palette dominated by saffron, off-white, maroon, rust orange and mustard yellow.
